r0.why: Definition, nonsquare n, hyperbola, integer points and trivial solution (1,0) all from [1],[2].

r1.why: Lagrange's infinitude [3], x/y approximates sqrt n [4], Baudhayana's 17/12 and 577/408 near sqrt 2 [14]; n = 2 follows from [4] with [14].

r2.why: 400 BC study of n = 2 for sqrt 2 [11], side and diameter numbers [13], Archimedes 1351/780 [15],[16], cattle problem [17].

r3.why: Brahmagupta circa 628 [5], triple definition [29], N = 92 worked example [25],[26], Bhaskara II 1150 general method [28], minimizing step [31], termination [32], N = 61 solution [33].

r4.why: 'In 1657 ... set it as a challenge ..., naming the cases N = 151 and 313 for John Wallis' ties the 151/313 challenge to the 1657 letter, which [35],[36] do not; [36] gives it only as Frenicle's report and says '151 or 313', not 'and'.

r5.why: Lagrange 1766-1769 theory via continued fractions and P + Q sqrt a [40], Brouncker-Wallis termination [41], fundamental solution from convergents [42]-[44].
